content.executive_insights:
- **Canonical Identity Confirmed**: Lead-036 is Robert W. Ebert, PhD, currently Lead Adjoint Professor and Assistant Director of the UTSA-SwRI Space Physics Graduate Program, and Principal Scientist in SwRI's Space Science and Engineering Division - https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert - meaning the lead-036 data sheet is directionally accurate and "Verified Identity" should be moved to confirmed.
- **Research Topic Coverage Is a 1:1 Match**: The seven current research items published on his official faculty page (solar wind spatial variations; solar wind interaction at Jupiter's magnetopause; energetic heavy-ion acceleration in interplanetary space; ion/electron dynamics at Jupiter; graphene-foil plasma and energetic neutral-atom instruments; SWiPS solar-wind plasma sensor; heliophysics/planetary mission concepts) map cleanly onto the input topics of solar wind, magnetospheric interactions, plasma mass spectrometry, and heliosphere - https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert - so the topic taxonomy is trustworthy.
- **SWiPS / SWFO-L1 Instrument Is the Strongest Direct Lead for 2024+ Funding**: An October 2, 2024 SwRI press release names Dr. Robert Ebert as the instrument PI for the Solar Wind Plasma Sensor (SWiPS), integrated onto NASA's NOAA-managed Space Weather Follow-On at L1 (SWFO-L1) - https://www.swri.org/newsroom/press-releases/swri-built-solar-wind-plasma-sensor-help-track-space-weather - but this is a mission/instrument build funded through NASA/NOAA, not a competitive research grant, and should be flagged as such in any CRM.
- **No Competitive Research Grants ≥ 2024-01-01 Are Publicly Attributable to Ebert**: Searches against the NSF Award Search, NASA Techport / ROSES solicitation list, USASpending, and NIH RePORTER did not surface a competitive grant award where Robert Ebert is named PI or co-I with a public dollar amount. Historical program lines (NASA Heliophysics Supporting Research; NASA Living with a Star) are documented only in a 2019 Scientia profile and pre-date the cut-off - https://www.scientia.global/dr-robert-ebert-pinpointing-the-physics-of-energetic-storm-particles-observed-in-near-earth-orbit - so this finding should be tagged "No verified public evidence found" rather than inferred.
- **Doctoral Admissions Are Open on a Rolling Cycle, Not a Single Hired-RA Posting**: The UTSA-SwRI joint PhD/MS program posts hard annual deadlines (PhD Fall = Jan 1, PhD Spring = Oct 1, MS Fall priority = March 1, MS Fall final = June 1) at https://grad.space.swri.edu/how-to-apply, and Research Assistantships covering stipend + tuition + benefits are described at https://grad.space.swri.edu/research-assistantship-description - but the RA is tied to admission, not a free-standing job posting, and is therefore not a classic "open position" of the type the request asked for.
- **LinkedIn Confirms Career Trajectory But Provides No Post-Level Hiring or Grant Evidence**: Robert Ebert's public LinkedIn profile (https://www.linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-20293133a) confirms the October 2024 step up to Assistant Director and an unbroken SwRI tenure since his 2010 postdoc, but no shuttered "post" content about grants, hires, or positions is publicly indexed - so LinkedIn is corroborative on identity and timeline only.
- **Email Discrepancy Is Real but Likely Cosmetic**: The official UTSA-SwRI faculty page publishes rebert@swri.edu (https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert), while the input sheet says rebert@swri.org. SwRI operates both domains, and mailing either should resolve; verify with a low-stakes ping before any automated outreach to avoid silent bounces.
- **Namesake Risk Is Manageable**: Four other "Robert Ebert" profiles surface on LinkedIn - Auburn Extension Animal Scientist, Ebert Appraisal President, Bay Area construction PM, BE General Contracting President - none share the space-physics CV, so disambiguation in CRM notes is sufficient rather than a re-verification effort.
content.1_identity_verification_and_disambiguati:
Lead-036 resolves to **Dr. Robert W. Ebert** in the UTSA-SwRI Space Physics Graduate Program directory, which is the canonical institutional source. The page at https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert lists him as "Lead Adjoint Professor and Assistant Director," employed by Southwest Research Institute, with research interests including (verbatim): "Ion and electron properties and dynamics in Jupiter's magnetosphere and auroral regions"; "Solar wind interactions at Jupiter's magnetopause"; "Solar wind physics: spatial variations and long-term trends"; "Origin, acceleration, and transport of energetic heavy ions in interplanetary space"; "Solar wind instrument development for Space Weather applications"; "Graphene foil technology for advanced plasma and energetic neutral atom instruments"; and "Mission concept development for heliophysics and planetary science." This profile makes him a 1:1 match against the four research topics the input sheet attributes to lead-036 (solar wind, magnetospheric interactions, plasma mass spectrometry, heliosphere). His terminal degree is a PhD in Space Physics from UTSA in Fall 2010, with an MASc Engineering Physics (University of Toronto, 2005) and a BS Physics (University of Calgary, 2003) per the same page.

A separate SwRI/UTSA profile at https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-rob frames him as the program's alumni and adds three pieces of biographical information not on the faculty page: a "UTSA Presidential Dissertation Fellowship" (2009), "NASA Group Achievement Award - Ulysses Mission Team" (2009), and "National Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC) of Canada Postgraduate Scholarship (PGS-D2; 2008-2010)." These are pre-2024 awards and sit outside the funding scope requested, but they corroborate the Canadian training path and early NASA instrument connection.

A 2019 Scientia magazine profile (https://www.scientia.global/dr-robert-ebert-pinpointing-the-physics-of-energetic-storm-particles-observed-in-near-earth-orbit) gives the most detailed narrative, identifying him as "Principal Scientist for the Space Science and Engineering Division at the Southwest Research Institute in San Antonio, TX" and "Assistant Adjoint Professor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy at the University of Texas at San Antonio." Scientia also names named collaborators (Maher Dayeh, Mihir Desai, Lan Jian, Gang Li, Charles Smith) and the modeling dependency "Particle Acceleration and Transport in the Inner Heliosphere (PATH)" for ESP physics, plus historic funding program lines of "NASA - Heliophysics Supporting Research" and "NASA - Living with a Star Research" that pre-date the 2024-01-01 scope and therefore cannot be claimed as active grants.

Namesake disambiguation is straightforward. Four distinct "Robert Ebert" public-LinkedIn profiles surface when searching without embedded keywords and none overlap with lead-036's space physics CV:

| Profile | Role | Why Not Lead-036 |
|---|---|---|
| Robert Ebert - linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-24a0ba40 | Extension Animal Scientist, Auburn University | Agricultural extension; no connection to space physics |
| Robert Ebert - linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-37156719 | President, Ebert Appraisal Service, Inc. | Real-estate appraisal industry; 1.9K followers, unrelated field |
| Robert Ebert - linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-66a59138 | Construction operations, Bay Area | Construction project management; no physics background cited |
| Robert Ebert - linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-2444b518 | President, BE General Contracting Inc. | Construction; 32 years in role |

Source URLs for the table: the LinkedIn URLs above plus the canonical SwRI profile at https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert. The disambiguation is therefore verified: lead-036 is unambiguously the SwRI space physicist, with no evidence that any of these four namesakes have any connection to UTSA or to NASA/SwRI mission work.

Email: the canonical page at https://grad.space.swri.edu/ebert-robert shows **rebert@swri.edu**, while the input sheet says **rebert@swri.org**. Both swri.org and swri.edu are operated by Southwest Research Institute; both should reach Ebert. Flag this as a low-priority reconciliation issue, not an identity issue.
content.2_recent_active_funding_announced_2024_0:
The most prominent recent item tied to Ebert is NOT a competitive research grant but a mission/instrument contract. The October 2, 2024 SwRI press release at https://www.swri.org/newsroom/press-releases/swri-built-solar-wind-plasma-sensor-help-track-space-weather states that "The Southwest Research Institute-developed Solar Wind Plasma Sensor (SWiPS) has been delivered and integrated into a National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) satellite dedicated to tracking space weather." The instrument PI is named as Dr. Robert Ebert; named team includes Prachet Mokashi and Michael Fortenberry. The instrument will be on the SWFO-L1 (Space Weather Follow-On at Lagrange 1) mission with NASA managing the mission for NOAA, and a planned launch of 2025. **The work is funded out of the SWFO-L1 mission contract flow, not a competitive research grant, and therefore should be tagged "Mission Funding (NOAA/NASA), not a research grant" rather than counted as a "grant" against lead-036.** Per the input rules, mission budgets and consortium funding must be distinguished from competitive grants, and this is one of those distinctions. No contract dollar amount was published.

A separate June 22, 2026 press release at https://www.swri.org/newsroom/press-releases/solar-wind-forecasting-will-help-define-heliosphere-s-boundaries covers related heliosphere work ("SwRI scientists are using a solar wind forecasting method combined with analytic and numerical heliosphere models to find out where the first plasma boundary of the outer heliosphere lies as NASA's New Horizons spacecraft hurtles toward the outer solar system"). The lead author of two papers is named as Dr. Jonathan Gasser (SwRI); Robert Ebert is NOT explicitly named in the excerpt of this press release. No dollar amount is published. The work does overlap with Ebert's stated mission concept interest but cannot be claimed as his funded grant.

A further June 29, 2026 press release at https://www.swri.org/newsroom/press-releases/nasa-s-new-horizons-research-team-extends-key-observations-of-interstellar-material-slowing-the-solar-wind extends earlier New Horizons / Voyager 2 / IBEX / IMAP solar-wind slowing science. Dr. Alan Stern is identified as the Principal Investigator of the New Horizons mission. Robert Ebert is not named in the body of this release in the source excerpts retrieved. No grant number or dollar amount is published.

For competitive grants from public award databases, the searches against NSF, USASpending.gov, NIH RePORTER, and the active NASA ROSES 2025 solicitations surfaced no award page that names "Robert Ebert" (or "Rob Ebert" / "R.W. Ebert") as PI or co-I after 2024-01-01. The hunt did return evidence that SwRI institutionally has active NASA Heliophysics-adjacent work (missions PUNCH, IBEX, IMAP are listed on https://www.swri.org/markets/earth-space/space-research-technology/space-science/heliophysics and https://www.swri.org/markets/earth-space/space-research-technology/space-science), but none of those pages tie specific funded award IDs to Ebert.

The prior research snapshot's CauseIQ hit (http://causeiq.com/organizations/southwest-research-institute%2C741070544) does report that "September 23, 2025. Received grants. Identified 8 new grant, including a grant for $390,619 from Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy." This is an institutional-level grant to SwRI as a whole, with no Ebert attribution in the source fragment. Treating it as Ebert-linked would be a conflation; it must be tagged as SwRI-wide.

**Finding (funding):** for competitive grants anonymously tied to Ebert after 2024-01-01, "No verified public evidence found." content.3_recent_and_open_positions:
Three categories of position need separate treatment.

**PhD/MS Admissions (posted, ongoing cycle, rolling acceptance).** The UTSA-SwRI Space Physics Graduate Program posts hard annual application deadlines at https://grad.space.swri.edu/how-to-apply: PhD Fall = January 1; PhD Spring = October 1; MS Fall priority = March 1; MS Fall final = June 1; MS Spring = December 1; MS Summer = May 1. Application fee is $50 ($90 for international). This is NOT a "hiring" posting in the conventional sense; it is an annual admissions cycle. A new cohort each year is admitted, and admitted students are eligible for Research Assistantships (see below). Verifying whether a specific 2026 cohort is still accepting Fall 2026 applications (likely yes, until Jan 1, 2027 for PhD) requires pulling the live page closer to the deadline; the current page text references "Academic Year 2024-2025" deadlines.

**Research Assistantships (described, eligibility tied to admission).** The page at https://grad.space.swri.edu/research-assistantship-description describes a program-eligible RA offering "a stipend, tuition, and the option of benefits" to qualified graduate students in the joint PhD/MS programs. The page was last updated in July 2026 (per source text). This is NOT a free-standing open requisition - it is a funding arrangement contingent on admission to the program, so it is more akin to a fellowship than to a posted job. Whether individual RAs are funded from Ebert's specific grants cannot be confirmed without program-leverage evidence.

**Standing open postings.** A direct check of the SwRI job-search portal (https://resapp.swri.org/ResApp/Job_Search.aspx) for Space Science positions surfaced no jobs in the retrieved snippets that are tied to Ebert; the careers landing page (https://www.swri.org/careers) is generic. Searches on ZipRecruiter (https://www.ziprecruiter.com/Jobs/Swri) and Indeed (https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Southwest-Research-Institute) turned up broader featured openings (e.g., "Faculty, Open Rank") that are not tied to Ebert's lab. **No Ebert-specific SwRI research engineer / research scientist / postdoc requisition was identified in the open hiring landscape during this research run; "No verified public evidence found" for any open posting between 2026-01-01 and 2026-07-11.** Searches covered the official resapp portal, the SwRI public careers page, ZipRecruiter, Indeed, and the UTSA Department of Physics and Astronomy pages (https://sciences.utsa.edu/physics-astronomy, https://catalog.utsa.edu/graduate/sciences/physicsandastronomy).

Closed/historical postings (≥2026-01-01) - "No verified public evidence found." Searches did not surface any archived SwRI/UTSA job posting for the Space Science or the Ebert subgroup that was posted on or after January 1, 2026 and has since closed. Searches on Indeed and ZipRecruiter did not bring back closed-archive entries for this person.

content.4_linkedin_evidence:
Robert Ebert's LinkedIn profile is at https://www.linkedin.com/in/robert-ebert-20293133a. The visible profile fields corroborate the canonical identity but do not contain public "post" content (LinkedIn's public view does not surface post bodies in this scrape; follower count is 0 in the captured data, which is consistent with posts being private or with this being a low-recrawl snapshot).

The career timeline on LinkedIn matches the institutional evidence: Assistant Director at SwRI (since October 2024); Lead Adjoint Professor at UTSA (since February 2020); prior SwRI progression - Staff Scientist (2022-2024), Principal Scientist (2019-2022), Senior Research Scientist (2017-2019), Research Scientist (2013-2017), Postdoctoral Researcher (2010-2013). His LinkedIn description reads: "Research on plasma and energetic particles in interplanetary space and Jupiter's magnetosphere and moon-magnetosphere interactions near the Galilean moons. Plasma instrument development. Business development. Assist with Department of Space Research management." As Lead Adjoint Professor his role expands to: "primary SwRI liaison for the joint Space Physics graduate program between SwRI and UTSA, advise graduate students, teach Space Physics graduate courses, and manage the adjoint faculty."

The October 2024 promotion to Assistant Director is the LinkedIn-side evidence most likely to be misread as a "hiring event" tied to lead-036, but it is in fact a title change for Ebert himself, not a posted research opening for someone else. No public posts were retrievable showing "we are hiring a postdoc" or "we received new NASA funding"; the LinkedIn profile is therefore corroborative on identity and career history, not on discrete hiring/grant transactions.

1. Treat lead-036 as a "verified identity - firm match" and graduate him from any "Researching" status.
2. In the funding cell of the CRM, populate one row for SWiPS/SWFO-L1 with a clear tag "Mission instrument funding (NOAA via NASA) - not a competitive grant," and one row each for the Jun 22, 2026 and Jun 29, 2026 New Horizons press releases with status "Confirmed Ebert involvement NOT established from public excerpts; treat as SwRI-institution science only."
3. Populate the hiring cell of the CRM with the UTSA-SwRI PhD admissions funnel as the primary channel (link https://grad.space.swri.edu/how-to-apply) and a separate row for the contingent Research Assistantship (link https://grad.space.swri.edu/research-assistantship-description). Do not invent a PhD/postdoc line item unsupported by sources.
4. Tag the email discrepancy as a minor reconciliation task, not an identity problem.
content.6_synthesis:
Across the four research dimensions required by the task (identity, post-2024 funding, hiring, LinkedIn evidence), the data converge on a consistent picture: lead-036 is the right Ebert, his research matches the lead topics almost perfectly, the only firmly documented 2024-or-after Ebert-attributable funding event is mission-instrument work on SWiPS for SWFO-L1, and his organization's only open hiring channel is a doctoral admissions funnel rather than a conventional job-board posting. That distinction matters more than the headline "SWRI is hiring" - if a recruiter runs a generic "PhD opening in space physics at SwRI" keyword alert they will miss the lead and the lead will miss them, because the actual mechanism is "apply to the UTSA-SwRI joint program by January 1 (Fall PhD)" and only then compete for an RA. The competitive research grant question has no positive public answer; the LinkedIn scrape returns career data, not transaction data; and the four namesake Robert Eberts on LinkedIn are cleanly distinguishable. The single unsourced premise (Was Ebert's research funded by a competitive grant after January 1, 2024?) returns "No verified public evidence found" - and that explicit verdict is more useful for downstream CRM decisions than a plausible-sounding inferral. Three dimensions explicitly contrast:

| Dimension | Strong evidence | Weak / no evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Identity | Faculty page + Scientia + alumni page + LinkedIn all converge on Robert W. Ebert at SwRI Space Science and Engineering Division | None - all sources agree |
| Funding (≥ 2024-01-01) | SWiPS/SWFO-L1 PI role (mission funding) | No competitive research grant ID, amount, or date publicly surfaced |
| Hiring | PhD/MS admissions funnel is open with hard annual deadlines; RA description is published | No free-standing job posting tied to his lab; no closed/historical posting tied to him since 2026-01-01 |
| LinkedIn | Career timeline corroborates institutional records; Assistant Director promotion Oct 2024 verified | No public posts about grants, hires, or collaborations surfaced |

The deepest cross-cutting insight is that lead-036's lab operates inside an institutional/program-channel hiring model rather than a lab-channel hiring model, while his external funding is delivered through mission contracts rather than competitive research grants. Operations and outreach should map accordingly: track new PhD admissions deadlines and SWFO-L1 program status (and successor missions like IMAP / SWFO-L1 follow-on), but do not chase NSF/NIH/USASpending grant records on the assumption that any will materialize - as of 2026-07-11, the publicly indexed grant record is not where lead-036's activity sits.
